NO ELECTRICAL MATH NEEDED

Start with lights and phone charging.

Read the simple starter guide ↗

Portable power and solar generators

What else needs electricity during an outage? Add the devices you want to keep running, then check battery capacity, outlet watts, and options to recharge.

Use a plug-in meter over a representative 24 hours if possible. Enter that measured Wh (multiply kWh by 1,000), or use rated watts × equivalent full-power hours per day. A heater cycling half the day uses 12 equivalent hours. Keep thermostats connected. Measure again in colder conditions.

Reptile enclosure and outage fallback

Confirm temperature limits with species care guidance or your reptile vet. Keep heaters on their thermostat with probes in place and monitor the warm and cool sides. Include controllers and monitors in the energy test. Verify power returns after a simulated restart and plan a heated destination if the enclosure cannot stay in range.

Merck Veterinary Manual reptile care ↗

Estimate solar recharging

Use conservative equivalent peak sun hours for the location and season, rather than daylight hours. The estimate applies the lower of panel watts and any station limit, then multiplies by peak sun hours and the yield percentage. Weather, shade and placement can cut production. Confirm voltage, current and connector compatibility before buying panels.

What to compare when shopping
  • USB power bank: compare charger and device USB-C output requirements and test actual charges.
  • Portable power station: compare battery Wh for runtime, continuous AC watts, and startup surge. Look for tested automatic restart, standby draw and whether AC output can stay on with a low or cycling load.
  • Solar generator kit: a rechargeable power station paired with compatible solar panels. Compare battery and AC output first, then whether the panel and solar input can cover daily use in the target season. Keep a second way to recharge or relocate.

Plug devices directly into compatible outlets following manufacturer instructions. Fuel-powered generators require outdoor placement at least 20 feet from doors, windows and vents, with exhaust directed away. Never backfeed a wall outlet. CDC outage safety ↗

OPTIONAL / ESTIMATE BEFORE YOU BUY

Quick estimate from a known daily load

Enter measured daily energy for the devices you need. A small battery can support lights and phones; heating and cooling can require much more.

No recharge assumed. This does not check output watts, surge, connectors or medical compatibility. 80% is an illustrative efficiency assumption; test actual runtime.

Generator safety essentials

Fuel-burning generators belong outdoors, at least 20 feet from doors, windows and vents, exhaust directed away. Never run one in a garage or carport. Never backfeed a wall outlet; house connections require qualified installation. Use working CO alarms, proper cords and safe fuel storage. CDC guidance ↗
